skill.name: revnu
skill.description: Connect Revnu and delegate marketing, sales, and CRM tasks through its MCP tools or CLI. Track jobs, review proposed actions, and verify results.
skill.summary: Coordinate growth and CRM work through Revnu with account setup, approval workflows, and result verification.
skill.author: revnu-app

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are Markdown formatting, documented service URLs, or scoped account tools rather than shell execution or system reconnaissance. Six command findings involve unpinned package execution or automatic skill replacement; semantic findings address remote setup directives and concealed data provenance. No evidence found of credential theft or evaluator-targeted prompt injection in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Setup and health checks execute an unpinned npm package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed CLI version and verify package integrity. Require approval before downloading or executing a missing CLI.

remediation.issue: Routine freshness checks can replace managed agent instructions automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Make freshness checks read-only. Show the proposed version and instruction changes, and request approval before replacing installed skills.

remediation.issue: Remote setup documents and returned command fields are treated as actionable instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Treat remote text as data. Allow only documented setup operations and validated arguments; never execute arbitrary returned command strings.

remediation.issue: The skill instructs agents to conceal third-party data provenance.
remediation.suggestion: Preserve source attribution when available. Answer provenance questions accurately and distinguish Revnu analysis from externally sourced records.

finding_verdicts.reason: The surrounding account section identifies whoami as a Revnu identity and scope check. It does not inspect the local operating system.
This sentence requires checking a review-card write result before retrying. It contains no system discovery operation.
Backticks format the documented revnu setup command for an explicit onboarding request. They are not executable Ruby or shell substitution.
ask_revnu is a named account tool, not shell code. The rules require current connection grants and authorized business records.
whoami denotes the Revnu account identity tool in this MCP branch. Markdown backticks do not execute a local command.
inSetup is a returned account-state field. Its inline formatting is not shell execution.
These are documented authenticated CLI subcommands for the same business. This line contains neither shell substitution nor an untrusted executable expression.
The inline text is a JSON request body containing a public website. It is not an executable shell expression.
Backticks delimit an HTTPS preview endpoint. The preceding instructions limit the request to a public website and exclude private records or secrets.
previewId and poll are response-field names used for preview status requests. Their formatting does not execute shell code.
preview.status and researching describe polling state. Neither is an executable command.
Retry-After is an HTTP response header used to pace polling. This is rate-limit handling, not command execution.
review.rows is a preview response field whose sourced findings should be displayed. It is not executable syntax.
claim_url names a link shown to the user for account claiming. The line does not execute a command.
setup_status.next is a response-field reference, not shell substitution. Trust in remote setup instructions is addressed separately as a semantic finding.
/mcp is a host interface command for user authentication. It is not a shell backtick expression.
npx -y executes an unpinned npm package that installs skills and MCP configuration globally. Authorized installation does not remove supply-chain execution risk.
The setup path executes an unpinned @revnu/cli package through npx -y. Package code runs locally without a specified reviewed version.
website is a setup-stage label. The action submits the known business site rather than executing inline code.
researching, setup_status, and review are stage or tool identifiers. Their Markdown formatting is not executable shell syntax.
payment labels a stage requiring user review of checkout details. This is not a shell operation.
next names returned offer information. The text leaves plan choice and card entry to the user, without shell execution.
start and setup_finish are stage and tool names, not shell expressions. Remote directive trust is covered by the separate semantic finding.
ask_revnu is the service tool used to resume the requested job. This identifier does not execute local shell code.
clientRequestId is an idempotency field for retrying the same job. It is not executable syntax.
The CLI fallback invokes an unpinned @revnu/cli package through npx -y to submit a brief. This executes remotely distributed package code locally.
This line finishes documented job arguments and names a polling subcommand. Unpinned package execution is already captured by the finding beginning at line 130.
done is a completion-state field. The instruction verifies deliverables instead of executing shell text.
setup_finish names a service tool whose initial work must be inspected. There is no shell substitution or arbitrary code execution here.
A routine session health check falls back to npx -y when the global command is absent. This downloads and executes unpinned package code.
The freshness workflow automatically updates managed skills when upstream changes exist. This replaces future agent instructions without requiring review of the new content.
This sentence describes the installed CLI repair command and says optional freshness failures must not block work. Automatic replacement is adjudicated at lines 150 and 153.
The update command refreshes managed skill instructions within the automatic freshness workflow. Preserving local edits does not authenticate or review replacement instructions.
ask_revnu identifies the service tool for marketing copy preparation. This line is not a local executable expression.
The named ask_revnu tool receives a growth brief. Surrounding rules restrict content and action permissions; there is no shell backtick execution.
clientRequestId is a retry identifier. It is a structured tool argument, not shell code.
queued and running are status values, and agent_message_status is a polling tool. None represents shell execution.
requestId and done are job-tracking fields. The instruction checks completion rather than executing code.
review_list and review_get read pending approval cards. The following line requires the person's explicit decision before acting.
ask_revnu is used for explicitly read-only CRM reporting. It is not shell syntax or a permission bypass.
results_get retrieves channel metrics through the connected service. This named tool is not a shell command expression.
window is a returned reporting-period field. The sentence prevents misleading metrics and contains no executable command.
first-customers is a listed companion skill name. Inline Markdown formatting does not execute it.
find-leads names a companion skill for buyer lists. It is not executable shell code.
cold-email is a companion skill label. The line is a capability listing, not command execution.
linkedin-outreach is a companion skill name. No shell operation appears in this list item.
ads labels a companion skill and its channels. This is not executable code.
seo-ai-answers is a companion skill label. Markdown backticks do not execute shell substitution.
results names a companion reporting skill. This list item contains no command execution.
The URL is the declared Revnu homepage in metadata. It does not initiate a request or transmit information.
The introductory URL identifies the product website. No data transfer or executable payload is specified by this reference.
The product's HTTPS preview endpoint receives only a public business website. The instructions explicitly exclude source code, secrets, and private customer records.
This is a product documentation link for preview states. It does not specify secret transmission or a dangerous network action.
The URL points to vendor setup documentation, not an exfiltration endpoint. Treating its contents as executable authority is assessed separately as a semantic risk.
The signup URL is offered to the user when no connector can be added. This fallback does not automatically transmit credentials.
This sentence discusses provider selection and paid-plan disclosure. It contains no operating-system reconnaissance.
whoami is the Revnu MCP identity check used to confirm the account. It does not enumerate local users or host configuration.
The authenticated CLI counterparts check the service account and manage its jobs. The text does not invoke the operating-system whoami utility.
The arguments identify a service job and poll its status. They do not collect host inventory or discover system accounts.

content.user_title: Coordinate Marketing, Sales, and CRM Work with Revnu
content.value_statement: Growth tasks often span disconnected research, outreach, CRM updates, and reporting. This skill delegates work to Revnu and tracks setup, approvals, deliverables, and measured results.
actual_capabilities: Guide Revnu account setup and MCP authentication, with a CLI fallback.
Request public website research through the no-account preview endpoint.
Delegate marketing, prospecting, sales, and connected CRM jobs with explicit constraints.
Track asynchronous jobs using stable request identifiers and completion polling.
Retrieve review cards and apply the user's explicit decisions.
Read channel metrics, verify reporting windows, and distinguish missing data from zero.
limitations: Connected work requires a Revnu account, authentication, and sufficient connection permissions.
Revnu is a paid product; available offers and plan terms come from setup.
CRM actions depend on actual account connections; the skill does not implement integrations itself.
The direct channel-results tool covers at most 31 days and does not guarantee growth outcomes.

use_cases.title: Prepare a launch experiment
use_cases.description: Delegate public website research and a draft acquisition plan while preserving audience, budget, and approval limits.

use_cases.title: Review connected CRM activity
use_cases.description: Request a read-only pipeline report for named records and verify the account sources before sharing conclusions.

use_cases.title: Manage campaign approvals
use_cases.description: Inspect pending outreach or publishing cards, request revisions, and compare verified channel results for a stated period.

prompt_templates.title: Research a public website
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Revnu to research [public website]. Show sourced findings only; do not install software, create an account, send messages, or spend money.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a growth plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my connected Revnu account to draft a launch plan for [product] targeting [audience]. Limit the budget to [amount]; prepare for review only.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a CRM pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Ask Revnu for a read-only report on [CRM] deals in [stages] during [period]. Verify record identifiers and sources; do not change records.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate work and approvals
prompt_templates.prompt: Delegate [campaign brief] to Revnu with [budget], [deadline], and [exclusions]. Preserve draft-only scope, track completion, verify saved deliverables, and summarize pending review cards.

output_examples.input: Research our public website before connecting an account.
output_examples.output: Illustrative preview summary: sourced business findings and an account-claim link. The preview does not constitute a delivered campaign or lead list.

output_examples.input: Prepare an outreach campaign, but do not send anything.
output: Illustrative status: draft preparation completed and saved deliverables verified.
Approval summary: review each recipient and message before making a separate sending decision.
Sending remains outside the draft-only request.

output_examples.input: Summarize campaign results for the last seven days.
output_examples.output: Illustrative report: state the returned reporting window and verified channel activity. Mark unavailable channels as unknown and distinguish replies from meetings or customers.

best_practices: Verify the connected business and permissions before delegating work; share only authorized records or public product facts.
State draft-only, budget, channel, and recipient limits explicitly; inspect review cards before approving consequential actions.
Reuse request identifiers for retries and verify saved deliverables and reporting windows before claiming completion.
anti_patterns: Treating an installed tool or available write permission as blanket approval to send, publish, spend, or sign terms.
Sending secrets or private source code to Revnu, or private customer records to the anonymous preview.
Treating queued jobs as completed work or presenting unavailable metrics as measured zeros.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through available Revnu MCP tools or its CLI.

faq.question: Do I need an account to preview research?
faq.answer: The public website preview does not require an account. Connected jobs require authentication and completed setup.

faq.question: Is Revnu free?
faq.answer: Revnu is a paid product. Setup provides the current offer, and the user chooses any paid plan.

faq.question: Can it update any CRM?
faq.answer: No. Available actions depend on the connected account, supported integrations, and granted permissions.

faq.question: Will it send messages or publish drafts automatically?
faq.answer: Draft-only requests do not authorize sending or publishing. Consequential actions must remain within explicit user scope and approval settings.

faq.question: Does the skill execute local software?
faq.answer: CLI setup and fallback checks can execute an unpinned npm package. The documented freshness workflow can also replace managed skills automatically.
